learning_extracted: A saturation-immune metric can still be defeated by a different upstream degeneracy: the 490k argmin-flip probe removed the 490j approach_commit_rate ceiling but was silently defeated by a range-zero per-candidate bias. Future modulatory-sufficiency probes MUST pre-register a bias-range>0 (input-non-degeneracy) guard, analogous to the headroom guard the 490j autopsy added.

MECH-295's per-candidate approach bias inherits the candidate-collapse and z_goal-collapse ceilings: with near-identical candidate z_world (SD-056 unfixed) and weak z_goal, goal_proximity is uniform across candidates, so the bias has zero range and cannot flip an argmin. This couples the MECH-295 behavioural retest to SD-056 + the GAP-2 foraging-competence substrate, not just to MECH-295's own gain.

The modulatory-bias-selection-authority substrate (landed 2026-06-03) is the named fix for 'fixed small modulatory magnitudes never change the argmin' -- but 490k ran with it OFF (default). The 490L retest must enable it (and SD-056 E2-contrastive) to give the bias argmin-competitive authority on a substrate where candidates are genuinely differentiated.

MECH-295 remains behaviourally unproven: substrate-firing support (493/490j) exists; behavioural-sufficiency support is still zero across the entire 490g/h/i/j/k lineage. narrow_supports_flag retained.
